event_time_meaning.uniform: each piece of the parent window carries 1/n of the event: 'stroke somewhere in this window, uniformly', which is the assumption cif_mid already declares, with no invented date (PRIMARY allocation of this arm)
event_time_meaning.last: the event in the parent's LAST piece - the convention the unsplit discrete-time likelihood implies, kept so the grid effect and the event-time effect can be told apart
event_time_meaning.midcell: the event in the piece containing the parent midpoint, later pieces dropped: the closest discrete-time reading of the declared midpoint date

note: each interval cut into ceil(L/delta) equal sub-intervals carrying the parent's start covariates; deaths and non-response tails keep their terminal status on the parent's last sub-interval because their t_end IS that date; a fractional event is emitted as a weighted 0/1 row pair in column row_weight
